chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who carried his slave upon an animal, so it trampled (someone). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The fine is upon his master'.
ai.seo_question: Who is liable for damages if an animal tramples someone while carrying a slave?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of financial compensation (ghurm) when a master utilizes his slave as a burden on an animal, ruling that liability rests with the master who directed the action. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between ownership and operational control, emphasizing that the one who benefits from or directs the animal's use bears the risk of damage. It serves as a foundational precedent for understanding vicarious liability in Islamic civil law.
